subject: Hospitality
title: Direct vs. Third-Party Bookings
description: A micro-lesson that makes Direct vs. Third-Party Bookings usable.

hook.text: When you book on Expedia, the hotel pays up to 25% commission. When you book on the hotel's website, they keep nearly everything.

buildup.text: Hotels invest millions in 'book direct' campaigns, promising best rates, free perks, and loyalty points for direct bookings.

discovery.text: Despite these efforts, OTAs remain dominant because they aggregate all hotels in one search. Convenience wins over loyalty.

twist.text: Hotels need OTAs for visibility—especially new properties. It's a symbiotic relationship they love to hate.

climax.text: The ideal mix? Hotels aim for 50–60% direct bookings and tolerate OTA commissions on the rest as a customer acquisition cost.

punchline.text: Direct saves money, OTAs bring eyes. Distribution is a balancing act.

quiz.question: Why do hotels tolerate OTA commissions?
options: OTAs provide visibility and act as customer acquisition channels
